note: Curated, deterministic post-processing maps keyed <sourceFormat>::<destFormat>. Structural field remap is compiled to chunked evals; the per-class dictionary (classMap) is generated into an editable in-pack CSV lookup so users extend the deployed pack without code. See CLAUDE.md and src/postprocess-builder.ts.

ocsf::cef.label: OCSF → CEF (ArcSight)
ocsf::cef.description: Transforms events already in OCSF (1.x) into ArcSight CEF. Reads OCSF's normalized objects (src_endpoint, dst_endpoint, actor.user, device, metadata, connection_info, traffic) into standard CEF extension keys — identical across every OCSF class. The CEF header (Name / DeviceEventClassID / severity) is resolved from an editable in-pack lookup keyed on class_uid, falling back to OCSF's self-describing class_name/type_name.

valueRules.cefSeverityFromOcsf: (__cls_sev != null && __cls_sev !== '') ? Number(__cls_sev) : (severity_level == null || severity_level === '' ? 0 : Number(severity_level) == 1 ? 1 : Number(severity_level) == 2 ? 3 : Number(severity_level) == 3 ? 5 : Number(severity_level) == 4 ? 7 : Number(severity_level) == 5 ? 9 : Number(severity_level) == 6 ? 10 : 0)

(http_request||{}).url : undefined) || (url && typeof url == 'object' ? url.url_string : undefined) || (typeof url == 'string' ? url : undefined) || uri || ((((http_request||{}).url)||{}).hostname && (((http_request||{}).url)||{}).path ? ((((http_request||{}).url)||{}).scheme ? (((http_request||{}).url)||{}).scheme + '://' : '') + (((http_request||{}).url)||{}).hostname + ((((http_request||{}).url)||{}).port ? ':' + (((http_request||{}).url)||{}).port : '') + (((http_request||{}).url)||{}).path + ((((http_request||{}).url)||{}).query_string ? '?' + (((http_request||{}).url)||{}).query_string : '') : undefined) || undefined

aliases.value: severity || (severity_level == 1 ? 'Informational' : severity_level == 2 ? 'Low' : severity_level == 3 ? 'Medium' : severity_level == 4 ? 'High' : severity_level == 5 ? 'Critical' : severity_level == 6 ? 'Fatal' : undefined)

ocsf::arcsight.label: OCSF → CEF (ArcSight, categorized)
ocsf::arcsight.description: The OCSF → CEF transform, plus ArcSight ESM categorization derived from OCSF's normalized taxonomy — a deviceEventCategory (cat) path and CategoryOutcome / CategorySignificance hints mapped from OCSF status_id and severity_id. Events land pre-categorized in ArcSight without a connector categorization file. Inherits the same editable class dictionary as the plain-CEF variant.

aliasesAdd.name: arcsight_significance
aliasesAdd.value: severity_level == null || severity_level === '' ? undefined : Number(severity_level) >= 5 ? '/Compromise' : Number(severity_level) >= 3 ? '/Suspicious' : Number(severity_level) == 2 ? '/Informational/Warning' : '/Informational'

ocsf::cim.label: OCSF → Splunk CIM
ocsf::cim.description: Re-normalize already-OCSF events into flat Splunk CIM (Network Traffic model) fields, rebuilt into a compact _raw JSON document. Reuses the shared OCSF→canonical alias step, then the same canonical→CIM golden mapping the raw-log pack flow uses — no separate CIM extension table to maintain.

ocsf::ecs.label: OCSF → Elastic ECS
ocsf::ecs.description: Re-normalize already-OCSF events into nested Elastic Common Schema objects (event / source / destination / network / user). Reuses the shared OCSF→canonical alias step, then the canonical→ECS golden mapping — the parent-object-first nested builder shared with the pack flow.

ocsf::asim.label: OCSF → Microsoft Sentinel ASIM
ocsf::asim.description: Re-normalize already-OCSF events into flat Microsoft Sentinel ASIM Network Session columns (SrcIpAddr / DstPortNumber / EventResult / EventSeverity). Reuses the shared OCSF→canonical alias step, then the canonical→ASIM golden mapping.

valueRules.asimSeverityOcsf: severity_level == null || severity_level === '' ? 'Informational' : Number(severity_level) == 2 ? 'Low' : Number(severity_level) == 3 ? 'Medium' : Number(severity_level) >= 4 && Number(severity_level) <= 6 ? 'High' : 'Informational'

ocsf::commonsecuritylog.label: OCSF → Microsoft Sentinel CommonSecurityLog
ocsf::commonsecuritylog.description: Re-normalize already-OCSF events into flat Microsoft Sentinel CommonSecurityLog table columns (DeviceVendor / DeviceProduct / SourceIP / DestinationPort / Activity / DeviceAction). Reuses the shared OCSF→canonical alias step, then the canonical→CommonSecurityLog golden mapping — the CEF-derived Sentinel table that Sentinel's Logs Ingestion API ingests as structured columns.

valueRules.cslSeverityOcsf: severity_level == null || severity_level === '' ? undefined : Number(severity_level) == 1 ? 1 : Number(severity_level) == 2 ? 3 : Number(severity_level) == 3 ? 5 : Number(severity_level) == 4 ? 7 : Number(severity_level) == 5 ? 9 : Number(severity_level) == 6 ? 10 : 0

ocsf::chronicle.label: OCSF → Google Chronicle UDM
ocsf::chronicle.description: Re-normalize already-OCSF events into nested Google SecOps UDM objects (metadata / principal / target / network / security_result). Reuses the shared OCSF→canonical alias step, then the canonical→UDM golden mapping. The shared step sets action from activity_name first (CEF act); UDM security_result.action is an ALLOW/BLOCK enum, so this delta re-derives action/outcome from OCSF's own disposition / action_id / status (untouched by the shared step).

aliasesAdd.name: action
aliasesAdd.value: disposition || (action_id == 1 ? 'allowed' : action_id == 2 ? 'denied' : undefined) || (disposition_id == 1 ? 'allowed' : disposition_id == 2 ? 'blocked' : undefined) || status || undefined

valueRules.udmSeverityOcsf: severity_level == null || severity_level === '' ? undefined : Number(severity_level) == 1 ? 'INFORMATIONAL' : Number(severity_level) == 2 ? 'LOW' : Number(severity_level) == 3 ? 'MEDIUM' : Number(severity_level) == 4 ? 'HIGH' : Number(severity_level) >= 5 && Number(severity_level) <= 6 ? 'CRITICAL' : undefined

ocsf::json.label: OCSF → Clean JSON
ocsf::json.description: Flatten already-OCSF events to normalized canonical JSON fields rebuilt into a compact _raw JSON document — the lowest-common-denominator destination when no vendor schema is required. Reuses the shared OCSF→canonical alias step, then the canonical→JSON golden mapping.
